FIELD.NAME: type
FIELD.COMMENT: global or user

FIELD.NAME: userid
FIELD.COMMENT: Owner of user-type preset

FIELD.NAME: rules
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON rules object

FIELD.NAME: warnings
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON warnings object

FIELD.NAME: scoring
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON scoring object

FIELD.NAME: review_link
FIELD.COMMENT: Review link

FIELD.NAME: archiveurl
FIELD.COMMENT: Archive url

FIELD.NAME: timecreated
FIELD.COMMENT: The time this record was created

FIELD.NAME: timemodified
FIELD.COMMENT: The time this record was modified

FIELD.NAME: timescheduled
FIELD.COMMENT: The time this record was scheduled

TABLE.NAME: availability_proctor_sess
TABLE.COMMENT: One proctoring session per quiz attempt, for the SDK proctoring model only. The hosted model uses availability_proctor_entries instead. This is the only forensic record of what happened during a session, because the SDK exposes no error channel.

FIELD.NAME: attemptid
FIELD.COMMENT: Nullable until the session binds to an attempt. The session is created before the attempt exists, because the learner is handed off to core's startattempt.php -- which runs the pre-flight chain (quiz password, SEB) and only then creates the attempt. See session::bind_attempt().

FIELD.NAME: sessionkey
FIELD.COMMENT: The sessionId JWT claim. 230 is the maximum the Developer Guide allows. Generated once and read back from this row on every relaunch -- never re-derived, because a reload must reuse the same sessionId.

FIELD.NAME: state
FIELD.COMMENT: pending, active, finishing, finished or abandoned. Transitions are one-way; see classes/session.php.

FIELD.NAME: reason
FIELD.COMMENT: Which SDK event drove the move to finishing or abandoned. The SDK has no error channel, so without this there is no record of why a session ended.

FIELD.NAME: timeactive
FIELD.COMMENT: When the JWT was signed and the session became active.

FIELD.NAME: timebound
FIELD.COMMENT: When the session bound to an attempt. The gap between timeactive and this is the window in which an active session is an unspent permission, so it is recorded to make that window auditable.

FIELD.NAME: timefinishing
FIELD.COMMENT: When examFinished resolved: recording stopped here, so anything after this timestamp is an unproctored tail.

FIELD.NAME: timefinished
FIELD.COMMENT: When the attempt was submitted. Submission alone drives the finished state.

FIELD.NAME: timeabandoned
FIELD.COMMENT: When appUnmounted resolved.

FIELD.NAME: videouploaded
FIELD.COMMENT: When videoUploaded resolved. Deliberately NOT a state condition: it can resolve after the row is already finished, and a finished row with a null value here is a reviewer signal (video may be incomplete), not a broken state.

FIELD.NAME: timefinishsent
FIELD.COMMENT: When the server-to-server finish request succeeded. Stops the request being repeated, and shows whether the recording was stopped by us on submission or by the learner pressing Finish exam.

FIELD.NAME: conclusion
FIELD.COMMENT: Proctoring conclusion from the result webhook: accepted, rejected or unknown. Null until a result arrives.

FIELD.NAME: score
FIELD.COMMENT: Proctoring score, 0-100. Null when the webhook omitted it, which is not the same as zero.

FIELD.NAME: comment
FIELD.COMMENT: Proctor notes from the result webhook.

FIELD.NAME: threshold
FIELD.COMMENT: The attention and rejected score thresholds, as JSON. Needed to interpret the score, since the boundaries are per-exam.

FIELD.NAME: reporturl
FIELD.COMMENT: Link to the session warnings report on the Constructor side.

FIELD.NAME: archiveurl
FIELD.COMMENT: Link to the video archive for the session.

FIELD.NAME: resultwarnings
FIELD.COMMENT: The warnings registered during the exam, as JSON. Named to distinguish it from the per-exam visibleWarnings setting, which is a different thing entirely.

FIELD.NAME: warningtitles
FIELD.COMMENT: Translated titles for the warning types, as JSON.

FIELD.NAME: sessionstart
FIELD.COMMENT: When proctoring started, as reported by Constructor.

FIELD.NAME: sessionend
FIELD.COMMENT: When proctoring finished, as reported by Constructor.

FIELD.NAME: timeresult
FIELD.COMMENT: When the most recent result webhook was accepted. The guide says Constructor repeats the call as fields become known, so this moves.

INDEX.NAME: attemptid
INDEX.COMMENT: Not unique: the column is nullable, and databases disagree on whether a unique index permits several NULLs -- MySQL allows it, and that difference must not decide whether two unbound sessions can coexist. One-session-per-attempt is enforced instead by the conditional UPDATE in session::bind_attempt(), which is portable and also settles the race between two simultaneous binds.

INDEX.NAME: quizid_userid_state
INDEX.COMMENT: Supports the open-session lookup: does this learner have a live session for this quiz?

TABLE.NAME: availability_proctor_deny
TABLE.COMMENT: Blocked access attempts under the SDK proctoring model. Detection only, never a control: it records that someone reached a guarded script without a valid session, after the fact. Separate from the session table because a denial can occur with no session row at all, which is the most interesting case, and because denials are high-volume and want pruning while session rows are evidence to keep. Note that this release ships no writer for this table -- see the note in classes/session.php::record_denial().

FIELD.NAME: attemptid
FIELD.COMMENT: Nullable: the attempt may not exist or may not be identifiable on the denied request.

FIELD.NAME: sessionid
FIELD.COMMENT: Session row involved, when there was one. No foreign key: the session row may be pruned while the denial record is kept.

FIELD.NAME: sessionstate
FIELD.COMMENT: Session state at the moment of denial, copied here so the record stays meaningful after the session moves on.

FIELD.NAME: reason
FIELD.COMMENT: no_session, state_pending, state_finished, sec_fetch_dest, not_owner or no_config.

FIELD.NAME: script
FIELD.COMMENT: Which entry point denied: attempt, summary or processattempt.

INDEX.NAME: attemptid_reason_time
INDEX.COMMENT: Supports the dedupe lookup, which asks for the most recent row with this attempt and reason.
